results.title: Sandbox provisioning latency (upstream #5321)
results.desc: CreateSandbox to Ready duration — the user-side of provisioning timeouts
results.prose: Upstream #5321 (breaking) makes compute provisioning and bootstrap timeouts configurable — acknowledging that provision time varies and operators need control over when to declare failure. I measured the user-side number those timeouts must bound: CreateSandbox to Ready on this gateway took 32.7s for a plain ubuntu sandbox (consistent with the 15-40s range across all our cycles). Timeouts configured below that envelope would generate false provisioning failures; the feature exists because this number is deployment-dependent.
results.steps: CreateSandbox; wait_ready with 180s timeout; record elapsed seconds.

results.title: Reconciler pod SecurityContext (control-plane conventions)
results.desc: Pod specs must drop ALL caps, no privilege escalation, runtime-default seccomp
results.detail: reconciler.go itself has 0 SecurityContext blocks (it delegates to resource builders); agent_runtime_resources.go:448-453 carries the full convention: AllowPrivilegeEscalation (bool var), Capabilities Drop ALL, SeccompProfile RuntimeDefault, RunAsNonRoot
results.prose: Random spec draw: standards/control-plane/conventions.spec.md — restrictive SecurityContext on every pod spec. My first grep targeted reconciler.go and found nothing — because the reconciler delegates pod construction to resource builders; the convention lives in agent_runtime_resources.go:448-453, and it's complete: AllowPrivilegeEscalation (defaulted false via variable), Capabilities Drop ALL, RuntimeDefault seccomp, plus RunAsNonRoot. This is the control-plane mirror of what we experience from inside sandboxes — the seccomp that blocks renderer forks and PTY allocation originates in exactly this posture. Convention verified live; my search was just aimed at the wrong file.
steps: Verify full block: Drop ALL caps, RuntimeDefault seccomp, RunAsNonRoot, no privilege escalation

results.title: Random env injection
results.desc: Two random env vars verified in exec
results.detail: [seed 1794333332] env round-trip: '' | 4th occurrence WITH settle delay — first-exec-of-battery-process pattern identified (TV-ENV and TV-FS fail in first-position only); warm-up exec is candidate fix
results.prose: Env round-trip returned empty for the FOURTH time — and this cycle disproves my first-exec race hypothesis: the 0.5s settle delay was in place, TV-FS (also exec-based) passed, yet TV-ENV's exec still came back empty. The raw-capture evidence from last cycle (6/6 clean retries) still holds, so the gateway responds consistently to retries. Revised hypothesis: intermittent empty response correlated with the FIRST exec issued in the battery process (both TV-ENV and TV-FS fail in first-executed position, whichever runs first in the sampled order) — likely an auth/session warm-up on the gateway's exec path. Harness fix candidate: a warm-up exec before the battery starts.
